sections.h2: Which Lincoln County office handles property tax?
sections.html:
The Lincoln County Tax Department, on the third floor at 100 East Main Street in Lincolnton, handles every step from listing to collection. It is split into five divisions: Land Records for mapping and 9-1-1 addresses, GIS, Appraisal, Listing, and Collections.

Appraisal staff answer revaluation and appeal questions at (704) 736-8670, and the Tax Administrator is responsible for listing, appraising and assessing real and personal property and for collecting the tax. The office also takes exemption and exclusion applications and assigns E-911 property addresses.

North Carolina taxes property at true market value, meaning the price a willing buyer and seller would agree on when neither has to act and both know the property's uses. The county applies the uniform appraisal standards in G.S. 105-283 to reach that figure.

sections.h2: When are Lincoln County property taxes due and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 and are considered delinquent after January 5 of the following year. When January 5 lands on a Saturday or Sunday, the deadline moves to the next business day.

A bill not paid in full by that date picks up a 2 percent penalty on January 6, then three-fourths of one percent interest on the first day of each following month until it is paid. The county says past-due accounts go straight to enforced collection under state law.

  • A 2 percent discount applies to payments made from July 1 through August 31.
  • Notices go out in early July to the owner of record as of January 1.
  • Commissioners set the tax rate by the end of June.
  • Partial payments are accepted, and prepayments toward next year can begin once the current bill is paid in full.
  • Cash, check, money order, debit or credit card and e-check are accepted, and cards and e-checks carry a convenience fee.

Mortgage companies do not get paper notices for escrow. Most lenders pull bill data from the county system, but an owner whose taxes are escrowed still receives a notice to keep.

sections.h2: When is the next Lincoln County revaluation?
sections.html:
Lincoln County reappraises every four years by resolution, and the next reappraisal takes effect January 1, 2027. The most recent one before that took effect January 1, 2023. State law requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, so the county's four-year cycle is shorter than the minimum.

The appraisal staff review qualified arm's-length sales since the last reappraisal, test them statistically, and build a Schedule of Values that the county commissioners approve. Sales between family members, between related companies, foreclosure sales and gifts do not always reflect market value, so they are not all used. The commissioners adopted the 2027 Schedule of Values, Standards, and Rules, and the county posts it for owners to read.

New value notices typically go out in February, and the informal appeal period opens the day they are mailed. Under the county's checklist, a new value should represent market value as of January 1 of the reappraisal year.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Lincoln County property value?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review, which must be requested within 30 days of the notice date printed on the reappraisal notice. You can email revaluation@lincolncountync.gov, use the online form, call (704) 736-8670, or write to the Appraisal Division at 100 East Main Street, Third Floor, Lincolnton, NC 28092.

If the informal answer does not satisfy you, file a written request with the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of the notice of the informal result. The board has five members and three alternates appointed by the commissioners, and its first meeting under G.S. 105-322 falls no earlier than the first Monday in April. You get a written decision within 30 days after the hearing.

The next step is the state Property Tax Commission, by written notice within 30 days of the board's notice, and after that the North Carolina Court of Appeals. An appeal can leave the value unchanged, lower it or raise it.

  • Good evidence: comparable sales on or before the valuation date, similar parcels with lower values, photographs and repair estimates.
  • Reasons the county lists as not grounds for appeal: high taxes, inability to pay, lack of county services, or the size of the increase.
  • Outside appraisals count only if dated before the valuation date, and the office does not recommend ordering one for an appeal.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Lincoln County?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three homestead programs, and an owner may use only one of them. Applications go to the county tax office on Form AV-9, and the state form instructions say the county must accept them through June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income at or below $38,800 for the 2026 tax year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent when income runs over the limit up to $58,200, with excess tax deferred, for owners who have lived in the home five years.

The county also runs a present-use value program for farm, horticulture and forest land. Qualifying tracts must be at least 5 acres for horticulture, 10 for agriculture and 20 for forest, and agricultural or horticultural land must average $1,000 of gross income a year over the previous three years.

sections.h2: What happens to Lincoln County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Taxes are ordinarily prorated at closing by the closing attorney, so the seller pays through the closing date. Check the settlement statement and ask your attorney or agent whether the proration was done if you are unsure.

An unpaid bill follows the parcel. Under G.S. 105-355 the lien attaches as of the listing date, and under G.S. 105-374 the county can foreclose it like a mortgage, with a sale at the courthouse door. A person who redeems before confirmation pays the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

Lincoln County counts 36,811 households with 2.50 people each, and 90.3 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so many sales involve owners who have been in place for years and carry exclusions or deferrals. Ask the Tax Department whether a circuit breaker or present-use deferral is attached before you list, because a disqualifying sale makes deferred taxes for the preceding three years come due.

faqs.q: When are Lincoln County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5. A 2 percent penalty starts January 6, followed by three-fourths of one percent interest each month.

faqs.q: Does Lincoln County offer a discount for early payment?
faqs.a: Yes, the county takes 2 percent off tax payments made from July 1 through August 31. Bills usually go out in early July.

faqs.q: When does the next Lincoln County reappraisal take effect?
faqs.a: The next reappraisal takes effect January 1, 2027, on a four-year cycle that followed the January 1, 2023 reappraisal. Value notices usually mail in February.

faqs.q: How do I start a Lincoln County property value appeal?
faqs.a: Request an informal review within 30 days of the notice date by emailing revaluation@lincolncountync.gov, calling (704) 736-8670 or writing to the Appraisal Division at 100 East Main Street, Third Floor, Lincolnton. A formal appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review follows within 30 days if you disagree.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Lincoln County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays through the closing date, because the closing attorney ordinarily prorates the bill at settlement. Any unpaid prior-year tax is a lien on the parcel and must be cleared at closing.
